Now I see the issue! At line 993:
```c
status = __glob (dirname, ..., &dirs);
```

This is a recursive call to `__glob` with `&dirs` as the `pglob`. The `dirs` is a local `glob_t` variable. Inside this recursive call, `dirs.gl_pathv` will be allocated.

Then at line 1000:
```c
status = glob_in_dir (filename, dirs.gl_pathv[i], ...);
```

This uses `dirs.gl_pathv[i]` which is a pointer to a string inside the `dirs` structure. But `glob_in_dir` may call `pglob->gl_pathv` realloc, which is `dirs.gl_pathv` in this case. Wait, no - `glob_in_dir` uses `pglob` which is the outer `pglob`, not `&dirs`.
